messages:
Mia: Heads-up — we've seen jitter in the observability ingress after the coalescer change. p95 trace ingestion latency spikes intermittently and it looks tied to the coalescer window (currently 25ms). Can we sync on SLA tuning and who owns this behavior?
Ashwin: Do you have a graph or a repro timeframe? link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/obs/ingest?orgId=1&from=now-1h to the last 2 hours would help. :eyes:
Mia: Yea, yesterday 18:12–18:45. Quick snippet of the config we rolled in v2.3: ```coalescer:
  window_ms: 25
  max_batch_bytes: 524288
  max_batch_items: 200
  ordering_guarantee: best_effort
```
Sam: We set 25ms intentionally to keep end-to-end latency down for hot paths. Tradeoff is higher CPU due to smaller batches + more syscalls. At 25ms batch fill rate is low at ~60% which is why CPU went up. Bumping to 50ms would improve tokens/sec and reduce GPU pressure.
Jess: If we bump window, we risk increasing tail latency for single-request flows. Can we do adaptive windowing? e.g., keep 25ms under low concurrency but widen at high qps. Also who should own the adaptive policy — ingest or platform? @Sam @Mia
Sam: Adaptive windowing makes sense. Ingest team can implement a simple feedback loop (target batch fullness ~85%). But platform needs to own rollout policy + SLO knobs.
Ashwin: Also callout: does changing batch window affect cost attribution? If events are merged differently we might change billing granularity and tenant attribution. We should avoid surprise bill diffs.
Mia: Good point — I ran a quick diff on a 10m slice. Larger windows reduce per-request metadata (less envelope overhead) -> ~3.4% token cost reduction, but dedup/merge semantics hid request boundaries in ~0.2% of traces. That could break downstream billing lookups if we key by span boundary.
Jess: OK action items: (1) small experiment with 3 configs, A: baseline 25ms, B: 50ms fixed, C: adaptive (25ms -> 100ms depending on fullness). (2) ingest implements best-effort to preserve request boundaries (tag merged batches with boundary markers) so billing can rehydrate. (3) platform owns rollout and SLO gates.
Sam: For monitoring, we should watch: p50/p95/p99 ingest latency, batch fill ratio, CPU%, token cost delta, "boundary-loss" count (how often boundary markers appear missing), and billing mismatch incidents.
Mia: I can define the evaluation PROM set and a tiny replay to validate correctness (no functional loss). I'll also attach the grafana panels I used.
deploy-bot: deploy v2.3 -> coalescer rollout started by @Sam at 2026-03-22T17:58:44Z :rocket:
Ashwin: Quick question — boundary markers sound like extra metadata. Will that increase token cost and negate the savings?
Sam: We can keep markers as a tiny binary flag in the envelope headers (negligible size compared to payload). Will measure in experiment.
Jess: I'll spin up the experiment tomorrow: create canary lanes for A/B/C with 2% traffic each and safe rollback if p95 > baseline + 10ms or boundary-loss > 0.5%. I'll post a short RFC follow-up with measurement sheets.
Mia: SG. Let's meet 30m tomorrow — 10:00 PT — 15m sync to finalize runbook. Who's in? :thumbsup:
Sam: +1
Ashwin: +1
Jess: +1
incidents-bot: Alert suppressed: ingest-p95-burst at 2026-03-21T18:20:27Z (no action after deploy)
Mia: Thanks all — I'll write the small playbook and upload the diff results to the RFC thread.
